subject: Staging runbook: sizing validation + Hosted→Dedicated cutover for HeliaHealth
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Park <megan.park@heliahealth.com>; CloudOps <cloudops@heliahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sizing for dedicated pool - initial numbers

Marcus — thanks for the call this morning. To recap our goals so the procurement and cloud teams can align: our product will move the main inference traffic from Redwood Hosted to a Dedicated pool at contract start (Dec 1). Our traffic profile: baseline ~12 requests/sec, typical response ~250 tokens, healthy bursts up to 30 rps during refine windows. P95 target is <= 450ms (we're generous on p99 but want < 1.2s).

Before we sign, we need an internal validation plan and a minimal staging cutover so we can verify behavior under our canonical prompts and privacy constraints. Can you share a runbook and a staged timeline for validation + roll back? Also please confirm whether the plan requires A100-80GB best-effort or if smaller A100-40GB with quantization is acceptable.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Director of AI Products
HeliaHealth
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>; Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>; Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sizing for dedicated pool - initial numbers

Sanjay — appreciate the clear profile. I attached a concise staging runbook (staging-runbook-v1.pdf) and our initial capacity estimate (capacity-estimate-8xA100.csv). High level recommendation: start with an 8x A100-80GB pool configured for mixed precision and int8 quantization for model variants where we’ve validated quality. Autoscale policy: base=8 GPUs, burst cap=12 for short spikes. Rationale: the 8-GPU baseline supports sustained 12 rps at 250 tokens/response while keeping p95 comfortably below 400ms on our perf tests for the 7B/13B variants.

Quick notes: we assume 70% cache hit rate for prompt prefixes (HeliaHealth templates), batching average 4 requests per batch during baseline. If your payloads have long histories, we should re-run the calculator.

I propose a 3-step validation:
- Stage (internal): run smoke + scripted evals against dedicated pool (3 hours)
- Load test (Redwood + Helia): 2 x 1-hour stepped blasts to peak (30 rps)
- Canary cutover: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 24-48 hours with rollback gates

I'll coordinate the runbook and canary checklist with Dev and Evelyn. If this looks ok, we can firm up dates for Nov 30 (staging) and Dec 1 (canary start).

Cheers,
Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>; Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: staging runbook: sizing validation + Hosted→Dedicated cutover for HeliaHealth

Adding the technical checklist from our infra team — pasted key items from the attached canary-checklist.md:

1) Pre-stage verification (Day 0):
   - Confirm model binaries & quantization build (sha256). Attachment: capacity-estimate-8xA100.csv lists build ids.
   - Validate KV cache warming: seed top 10k prefixes.
   - Confirm KMS/HSM key access and audit logging enabled for pool.

2) Staging smoke (2–3 hours):
   - Run canonical prompt set (200 prompts) with golden answers and record token-accuracy regressions. Threshold: < 1.5% deviation in correctness metrics.
   - Observe batching rates and token throughput. Check p50/p95/p99 latencies.

3) Load test (same day):
   - Step ramp: 5 rps -> 12 rps -> 20 rps -> 30 rps, hold 10m each.
   - Monitor error-rate, queue depth, tail-latency and GPU mem pressure.

4) Canary window (cutover day):
   - Traffic ramp: 2% (2h) -> 10% (4h) -> 50% (8h) -> 100% (overnight).
   - Rollback gate: any sustained p95 increase >20% or error-rate >0.5% triggers immediate rollback to Hosted.

5) Post-cutover (24–72h):
   - Cost telemetry check vs forecast. Confirm autoscale triggers.
   - Final sign-off and DocuSign commit.

Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

P.S. For the A100 variant question: we can operate on 40GB instances with more aggressive quantization but we recommend 80GB for the initial canary to reduce risk and simplify caching behavior.
From: Megan Park <megan.park@heliahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliahealth.com>, CloudOps <cloudops@heliahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: staging runbook: sizing validation + Hosted→Dedicated cutover for HeliaHealth

Thanks team — this looks good. A couple of Clarifications from our CloudOps:
- Can you add a short verification step to confirm request-level provenance headers are preserved when traffic is routed to Dedicated? We need this for our audit trail.
- For the KV cache seeding, can you provide the script or a small CSV of the top 2k prefixes we should seed?

Also, given our procurement timelines, if the canary completes successfully on Dec 1 we will sign the reserved capacity and trigger payment terms. We are OK with starting the canary on Dec 1 but would like a short maintenance window at 01:00–03:00 UTC if any final binary roll is required.

Megan
Head of CloudOps, HeliaHealth
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Megan Park <megan.park@heliahealth.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliahealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Finalized staging dates & cutover timeline (Nov 30–Dec 2)

All — quick status and finalized timeline after last sync:

- Nov 30 (Tue) 18:00–22:00 PST: Staging & smoke tests in HeliaHealth sandbox. Actions: Redwood infra to deploy dedicated pool (8x A100-80GB), seed KV cache, run 200 canonical prompts.
- Dec 1 (Wed) 01:00–03:00 UTC: optional maintenance window for final binary swap (agreed by Helia).
- Dec 1 12:00 PST: Canary kick-off — traffic ramp plan below; primary owners on-call: Dev and Helia CloudOps.
   * 12:00–14:00 PST: 2% traffic
   * 14:00–18:00 PST: 10% traffic
   * 18:00–02:00 PST (overnight): 50% traffic
   * Dec 2 08:00 PST: Full 100% cutover if metrics stable

Rollback gates (trigger immediate rollback to Hosted):
- p95 latency above 20% vs baseline for more than 15 minutes
- error-rate > 0.5% for more than 5 minutes
- any audit/tracing header loss observed

Deliverables before Nov 30:
- Redwood: runbook + canary-checklist.md (attached), capacity csv, model build hashes.
- Helia: top-2k prefix CSV for KV warm and contact windows for CloudOps.

I'll open a HubSpot task and a shared Drive folder with all artifacts (link in metadata). Once the canary completes and Helia signs, we'll finalize the reserved capacity DocuSign.

Thanks — excited to get Helia onto Dedicated and reduce your cost-per-token while preserving latency.

Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: staging-runbook-v1.pdf (26 pages), capacity-estimate-8xA100.csv (CSV), canary-checklist.md (markdown)
